about: How a step of a school unit's introduction is read aloud (companion/COURSE.md, "Read aloud"): inputs (an intro as a unit has it, rendered for the learner; the learner's pair; the texts the voice store has a clip of, with their voice) and what is read, in the teacher's voice (slovene) or the phone's. The app (data/IntroSpeech.kt: IntroSpeechParityTest) and the bridge's port (src/course-speech.ts: the smoke's course-speech section) read these same cases, so voice-build voices ahead exactly what the app reads. A mark: whole, part:<line>:<from>-<to>, example:<i>, question, answer. Regenerate the expected values only from a change made on both sides.

intros.name: biti in English: the forms in bold, the intro's own words ("Biti"), a tap choice with its options said, a gap, the grammar page's rule as the summary (paragraphs)
intros.title: Biti: sem, si, je

say.en: **Biti** (to be) has a short form for each person, and Slovene never leaves it out. One person first: **jaz sem** (I am), **ti si** (you are), **on, ona, ono je** (he, she, it is). The pronoun is usually dropped: the form already says who.
say.de: **Biti** (sein) hat für jede Person eine kurze Form, und das Slowenische lässt es nie weg. Zuerst eine Person: **jaz sem** (ich bin), **ti si** (du bist), **on, ona, ono je** (er, sie, es ist). Das Pronomen fällt meist weg: Die Form sagt schon, wer.
say.it: **Biti** (essere) ha una forma breve per ogni persona, e lo sloveno non lo omette mai. Prima una persona: **jaz sem** (io sono), **ti si** (tu sei), **on, ona, ono je** (lui, lei, esso è). Il pronome di solito cade: la forma dice già chi.

examples.en: Granny Micka is in the kitchen.
examples.de: Oma Micka ist in der Küche.

ask.explain: Luka is one person, on (he): **je**. Luka je na pašniku: Luka is on the pasture.

say.en: Three or more: **mi smo** (we are), **vi ste** (you are: several of you, or one person you say vi to), **oni so** (they are). Three words to learn: **smo, ste, so**.
say.de: Drei oder mehr: **mi smo** (wir sind), **vi ste** (ihr seid, oder eine Person, die man siezt), **oni so** (sie sind). Drei Wörter zum Lernen: **smo, ste, so**.
say.it: Tre o più: **mi smo** (noi siamo), **vi ste** (voi siete, o una persona a cui si dà del Lei), **oni so** (loro sono). Tre parole da imparare: **smo, ste, so**.

examples.en: The children are in the garden.

ask.explain: Otroci (the children) are three or more, oni: **so**.

say.en: Slovene has a form for exactly **two**, the dual (dvojina): **midva sva** (we two are), **vidva sta** (you two are), **onadva sta** (the two of them are). Two people with *in* (and) take it too: **Luka in Tine sta …**
say.de: Das Slowenische hat eine Form für genau **zwei**, den Dual (dvojina): **midva sva** (wir zwei sind), **vidva sta** (ihr zwei seid), **onadva sta** (die zwei sind). Zwei Personen mit *in* (und) nehmen sie auch: **Luka in Tine sta …**
say.it: Lo sloveno ha una forma per esattamente **due**, il duale (dvojina): **midva sva** (noi due siamo), **vidva sta** (voi due siete), **onadva sta** (loro due sono). Anche due persone con *in* (e) la prendono: **Luka in Tine sta …**

examples.sl: Luka in Tine sta pri ribniku.
examples.en: Luka and Tine are by the pond.
examples.de: Luka und Tine sind am Teich.
examples.it: Luka e Tine sono allo stagno.

ask.explain: Micka and France are two: **sta**. Three or more would be *so*.

say.en: To say **no**, *ne* and the form melt into one word: **nisem, nisi, ni**; **nismo, niste, niso**; for two **nisva, nista**. Never *ne sem*.
say.de: Für **nein** verschmelzen *ne* und die Form zu einem Wort: **nisem, nisi, ni**; **nismo, niste, niso**; für zwei **nisva, nista**. Nie *ne sem*.
say.it: Per dire **no**, *ne* e la forma si fondono in una parola: **nisem, nisi, ni**; **nismo, niste, niso**; per due **nisva, nista**. Mai *ne sem*.

ask.explain: je → **ni**: Babica ni doma, je na vrtu (Granny isn't at home, she's in the garden).

rule.en:
**Biti** (to be) is the verb you need most, and Slovene never leaves it out: **Moja partnerka je iz Gorice.**

Its present: **sem, si, je**; **smo, ste, so**; for two: **sva, sta, sta**. The pronoun is usually dropped, because the ending already tells who: **Sem Jan.**

The negative fuses **ne** with the verb into one word: **nisem, nisi, ni, nismo, niste, niso** (for two: **nisva, nista**).

The short forms lean on the word before them (see the page on clitics): **Jan je doma.** A sentence may also start with them: **Sem Jan.**
rule.de:
**Biti** (sein) ist das wichtigste Verb, und das Slowenische lässt es nie weg: **Moja partnerka je iz Gorice.** (Meine Partnerin ist aus Gorizia.)

Sein Präsens: **sem, si, je**; **smo, ste, so**; für zwei: **sva, sta, sta**. Das Pronomen fällt meist weg, weil die Endung schon sagt, wer: **Sem Jan.**

Die Verneinung verschmilzt **ne** mit dem Verb zu einem Wort: **nisem, nisi, ni, nismo, niste, niso** (für zwei: **nisva, nista**).

Die kurzen Formen lehnen sich an das Wort davor (siehe die Seite über Klitika): **Jan je doma.** Ein Satz darf auch mit ihnen beginnen: **Sem Jan.**
rule.it:
**Biti** (essere) è il verbo che serve di più, e lo sloveno non lo omette mai: **Moja partnerka je iz Gorice.** (La mia compagna è di Gorizia.)

Il presente: **sem, si, je**; **smo, ste, so**; per due: **sva, sta, sta**. Il pronome di solito cade, perché la desinenza dice già chi: **Sem Jan.**

La negazione fonde **ne** con il verbo in una sola parola: **nisem, nisi, ni, nismo, niste, niso** (per due: **nisva, nista**).

Le forme brevi si appoggiano alla parola precedente (vedi la pagina sui clitici): **Jan je doma.** Una frase può anche cominciare con loro: **Sem Jan.**

goal.en: You can say who you are, where people are, and that they aren't.
goal.de: Du kannst sagen, wer du bist, wo Leute sind und dass sie es nicht sind.
goal.it: Sai dire chi sei, dove sono le persone e che non ci sono.

say.en: Every Slovene noun is **masculine**, **feminine** or **neuter** (spol). You can hear it at the end of the word. Words in **-a** are feminine: **miza** (table), **hiša** (house), **kava** (coffee).
say.de: Jedes slowenische Nomen ist **männlich**, **weiblich** oder **sächlich** (spol). Man hört es am Ende des Wortes. Wörter auf **-a** sind weiblich: **miza** (Tisch), **hiša** (Haus), **kava** (Kaffee).
say.it: Ogni nome sloveno è **maschile**, **femminile** o **neutro** (spol). Lo senti alla fine della parola. Le parole in **-a** sono femminili: **miza** (tavolo), **hiša** (casa), **kava** (caffè).

say.en: Words that end in a **consonant** are masculine: **kruh** (bread), **stol** (chair), **šotor** (tent).
say.de: Wörter, die auf einen **Konsonanten** enden, sind männlich: **kruh** (Brot), **stol** (Stuhl), **šotor** (Zelt).
say.it: Le parole che finiscono in **consonante** sono maschili: **kruh** (pane), **stol** (sedia), **šotor** (tenda).

- **Živjo** to a friend ✨
• **Zdravo** too
* *Adijo* when you go
1. First **jutro**
2) Then **večer**
---
| a | b |
|---|---|
   
**Nemčija** → **iz Nemčije**, see `-ija`, **bold *in* it**, and **hello** stays English.	Tabs and  spaces.
A gap you type: **Kako ste?** to someone you say *vi* to. 1) **Kako si?** to a friend.
